title: CS1-LD2RT: amplification by repetition and plurality of CS1-LD2R - tolerance 1/(2*10^10 n^4) under the adaptive malformed-copy model, time n^5 log2 n 2^(n/(2 log2 n)), polynomial source copies O(n^4)

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single CS1-LD2RT algorithm and configuration of proof.md (for n >= 64: G = 2^23 + 1 independent complete runs of the log-depth linear-merge collimation algorithm CS1-LD2R of Part I and the plurality of their G answers; for n < 64: the finite acquire-all-then-permute threshold test of Section 18) outputs the entire s with probability at least 1 - 2^-60 > 2/3 under the adaptive malformed-copy model of the fifth claim with tolerated fraction epsilon(n) = 1/(2*10^10 n^4), for every admissible adversary (including the one that corrupts nothing), and on EVERY execution branch, for every such adversary, including all failures, retries, discards and aborts, its total charged sequential work is T(N,s) = O(n^5 (log2 n) 2^(n/(2 log2 n))), with the uniform bit-length envelope B_T(n) = n^5 (log2 n) 2^(n/(2 log2 n)), whose exact growth index is 1. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N, s, outcomes and the adversary. This holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and the tolerance claim for the same execution.

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single CS1-LD2RT algorithm and configuration of proof.md (for n >= 64: G = 2^23 + 1 independent complete runs of the log-depth linear-merge collimation algorithm CS1-LD2R of Part I and the plurality of their G answers; for n < 64: the finite acquire-all-then-permute threshold test of Section 18) outputs the entire s with probability at least 1 - 2^-60 > 2/3 under the adaptive malformed-copy model of the fifth claim with tolerated fraction epsilon(n) = 1/(2*10^10 n^4), for every admissible adversary (including the one that corrupts nothing), and on EVERY execution branch, for every such adversary, including all failures, retries, discards and aborts, its peak classical workspace is S_C(N,s) = O(n (log2 n)^2 2^(n/(2 log2 n))) bits, with envelope B_C(n) = n (log2 n)^2 2^(n/(2 log2 n)), whose exact growth index is 1. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N, s, outcomes and the adversary. This holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and the tolerance claim for the same execution.

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single CS1-LD2RT algorithm and configuration of proof.md (for n >= 64: G = 2^23 + 1 independent complete runs of the log-depth linear-merge collimation algorithm CS1-LD2R of Part I and the plurality of their G answers; for n < 64: the finite acquire-all-then-permute threshold test of Section 18) outputs the entire s with probability at least 1 - 2^-60 > 2/3 under the adaptive malformed-copy model of the fifth claim with tolerated fraction epsilon(n) = 1/(2*10^10 n^4), for every admissible adversary (including the one that corrupts nothing), and on EVERY execution branch, for every such adversary, including all failures, retries, discards and aborts, its peak quantum workspace is S_Q(N,s) = O(n) qubits, with envelope B_Q(n) = n, whose exact growth index is 0. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N, s, outcomes and the adversary. This holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and the tolerance claim for the same execution.

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single CS1-LD2RT algorithm and configuration of proof.md (for n >= 64: G = 2^23 + 1 independent complete runs of the log-depth linear-merge collimation algorithm CS1-LD2R of Part I and the plurality of their G answers; for n < 64: the finite acquire-all-then-permute threshold test of Section 18) outputs the entire s with probability at least 1 - 2^-60 > 2/3 under the adaptive malformed-copy model of the fifth claim with tolerated fraction epsilon(n) = 1/(2*10^10 n^4), for every admissible adversary (including the one that corrupts nothing), and on EVERY execution branch, for every such adversary, including all failures, retries, discards and aborts, the total number Q(N,s) of source copies acquired, counting every discarded, rejected and failed-attempt copy, every malformed copy and the padding copies, is exactly 400 N on the branch n < 64 (a finite number depending on N only) and exactly Qtot(n) = (2^23 + 1) * 4050000000 n^4 on the branch n >= 64. Hence Q(N,s) = O(n^4) with envelope B_samples(n) = n^4, whose exact growth index is 0. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N, s, outcomes and the adversary. This holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and the tolerance claim for the same execution.

Fractional error tolerance epsilon(n) = 1/(2*10^10 n^4), for every N >= 2 (no validity threshold) and every s, under the adaptive malformed-copy model of the error_model text (proof.md Section 16): with Q acquired copies at most floor(epsilon(n) Q) are malformed; the adversary knows N, s, the algorithm and every measurement outcome obtained before each delivery and chooses adaptively which copies are malformed; malformed copies are arbitrary (n+1)-qubit states, possibly entangled with one another and with the adversary's system but not with clean copies or the algorithm's workspace; every other copy is, at delivery, an independent ideal coset state in tensor product with everything else; the adversary has no access after delivery. For every such adversary, including the one that corrupts nothing (the clean problem), CS1-LD2RT outputs the entire s with probability at least 1 - 2^-60 > 2/3 (proof.md Theorem RT), jointly with the four resource bounds of the first four claims, which hold on every branch. The fraction bounds the number of malformed copies among acquired copies; it is not a per-copy corruption probability. The tolerance is obtained by independent repetition and plurality of a clean algorithm; no robustness of the trees, the decoder or the label extraction is claimed.

structured.error_model: Adaptive malformed-copy model with fraction epsilon(n). Parameters: N >= 2 is the modulus, s in Z/NZ the secret, n = ceil(log2 N), Q the total number of source copies the algorithm acquires, and epsilon(n) the tolerated malformed fraction. Copies are delivered one at a time in acquisition order j = 1, ..., Q. Before copy j is delivered, an adversary that knows N, s, the full description of the algorithm, and every measurement outcome the algorithm obtained before copy j is delivered, and that may hold, process and measure an arbitrary private quantum system, decides adaptively whether copy j is malformed; on every execution branch at most floor(epsilon(n) Q) of the Q acquired copies are malformed. A malformed copy is an arbitrary (n+1)-qubit state (the register shape of an ideal copy) supplied from the adversary's system: it may be pure or mixed, may be entangled with the adversary's remaining system and with other malformed copies, and may depend on all of the information above; it is not entangled with clean copies or with the algorithm's workspace, ancillas or internal random bits. Every copy that is not malformed is clean: at the moment of its delivery, a fresh ideal coset state rho_s = (1/N) sum_x |psi_{x,s}><psi_{x,s}| in tensor product with everything else (the adversary's system, all other copies and the algorithm's workspace), i.e. clean copies are independent ideal coset states. The adversary interacts with the algorithm only by supplying copies; after delivery it has no access to the copy or to the algorithm's quantum or classical systems. All measurements have countably many outcomes. The algorithm is not told which copies are malformed. Quantifiers: the guarantee must hold for every N >= 2 (no validity threshold), every s in Z/NZ and every such adversary, including the adversary that corrupts nothing (the clean problem): the algorithm outputs the entire s with probability at least 2/3, and the four declared resource bounds hold on every execution branch. The fraction bounds the number of malformed copies among acquired copies; it is not a per-copy corruption probability.
